❗️AI was supposed to kill a million jobs. It may have created them instead.

The Economist estimates the AI boom has added around 1 million jobs in the US above normal employment trends.

Yes, about 200,000 jobs have disappeared since mid-2023 in roles where companies cited AI.

But the bigger surprise is where the new jobs are coming from.

Electricians. HVAC technicians. Construction crews. Utility workers. The people building the massive data centers and power infrastructure AI needs.

Then there’s the obvious wave of engineers, software developers, data scientists and AI specialists.

The estimate isn’t a perfect government count, but the trend is interesting: AI isn’t just replacing workers. It’s creating an entire economy around itself.

posts.text:
Li River, China 🇨🇳

Winding through dreamlike karst formations, the Li River forms the soul of Guilin. Towering limestone peaks pierce the surface of the water like ancient stone sentinels, often veiled in mist, transforming the valley into a living scroll painting.

Tranquil, reflective, and rich with atmosphere, the river reveals its magic at a slow pace — best enjoyed drifting on a bamboo raft or cruising between Guilin and Yangshuo. Water buffalo graze along the banks, fishermen cast nets with trained cormorants, and each turn of the river unveils another scene worthy of a postcard.

The Li River isn’t just scenic — it’s serene, ageless, and quietly emblematic of China’s natural grace.
